subject: renege_in doesn't set finished to FALSE if trajectory() is used

messages.author: 02c504fc23f1bb98
messages.subject: renege_in doesn't set finished to FALSE if trajectory() is used
parts:
Two opening statements; 1) what a great package!! 2) new user so I hope my question is not ignorant... :)

I'm running the following example code inspired from the bank tutorial. I use renegade_in() below in its simplest form (see bold comment in code) to simulate a customer leaving after a period of time. 

## leave with some probability
set.seed(1234)

traj <- trajectory() %>%
  log_("leave with some probability") %>%
  leave(function() runif(1) < 0.5) %>%
  log_("didn't leave")

simmer() %>%
  add_generator("dummy", traj, at(0, 1)) %>%
  run() %>% invisible#> 0: dummy0: leave with some probability
#> 1: dummy1: leave with some probability
#> 1: dummy1: didn't leave
## reneging after some time
bank <- trajectory() %>%
  log_("here I am") %>%
  # renege in 5 minutes
  renege_in(5) %>%    # I changed this from the example on the website
  seize("clerk") %>%
  # stay if I'm being attended within 5 minutes
  renege_abort() %>%
  log_("I'm being attended") %>%
  timeout(10) %>%
  release("clerk") %>%
  log_("finished")

cc <- simmer() %>%
  add_resource("clerk", 1) %>%
  add_generator("customer", bank, at(0, 1)) %>%
  run() #> 0: customer0: here I am

arrivals <- get_mon_arrivals(cc)
arrivals

> arrivals
       name start_time end_time activity_time finished replication
1 customer1          1        6             0    FALSE           1
2 customer0          0       10            10     TRUE           1

This is what I expect. I'm interested in the "finished" column as I'm learning to model a Call centre and can easily compute expected abandonment rates through it.

However, when I change the renege_in() command to: "renege_in(5, out = trajectory() %>% log_("lost my patience. Reneging..."))" as per website example I get the following:

set.seed(1234)

traj <- trajectory() %>%
  log_("leave with some probability") %>%
  leave(function() runif(1) < 0.5) %>%
  log_("didn't leave")

simmer() %>%
  add_generator("dummy", traj, at(0, 1)) %>%
  run() %>% invisible#> 0: dummy0: leave with some probability
#> 1: dummy1: leave with some probability
#> 1: dummy1: didn't leave
## reneging after some time
bank <- trajectory() %>%
  log_("here I am") %>%
  # renege in 5 minutes
  renege_in(5, out = trajectory() %>% log_("lost my patience. Reneging...")) %>%
  seize("clerk") %>%
  # stay if I'm being attended within 5 minutes
  renege_abort() %>%
  log_("I'm being attended") %>%
  timeout(10) %>%
  release("clerk") %>%
  log_("finished")

cc <- simmer() %>%
  add_resource("clerk", 1) %>%
  add_generator("customer", bank, at(0, 1)) %>%
  run() #> 0: customer0: here I am

Output: 
0: customer0: here I am
0: customer0: I'm being attended
1: customer1: here I am
6: customer1: lost my patience. Reneging...
10: customer0: finished


arrivals <- get_mon_arrivals(cc)
arrivals

       name start_time end_time activity_time finished replication
1 customer1          1        6             0     TRUE           1
2 customer0          0       10            10     TRUE           1

This is not what I expect. The reference page for renege says: "Arrivals that leave the trajectory will set the finished flag to FALSE in the output of get_mon_arrivals. "

Am I misunderstanding how things work, or is there a challenge with logging of renege tasks?

Many thanks!
Martin

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] renege_in doesn't set finished to FALSE if trajectory() is used
parts:
On Sun, 26 Jul 2020 at 07:35, Xistance <martijn...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Two opening statements; 1) what a great package!! 2) new user so I hope my question is not ignorant... :)
Thanks! The only "ignorant" question is the one never asked. :)

> I'm running the following example code inspired from the bank tutorial. I use renegade_in() below in its simplest form (see bold comment in code) to simulate a customer leaving after a period of time.
>

>
> However, when I change the renege_in() command to: "renege_in(5, out = trajectory() %>% log_("lost my patience. Reneging..."))" as per website example I get the following:
>

> name start_time end_time activity_time finished replication
> 1 customer1 1 6 0 TRUE 1
> 2 customer0 0 10 10 TRUE 1
>
> This is not what I expect. The reference page for renege says: "Arrivals that leave the trajectory will set the finished flag to FALSE in the output of get_mon_arrivals. "

This is expected behaviour. In this case, the arrival is not leaving
the trajectory "unexpectedly" anymore, because you are redirecting it
to a fallback trajectory. The same happens if you use
handle_unfinished(), in a more general way, to catch any abandoning
customer.

If you still want those to be marked as not finished, then simply
chain a leave(1) activity after the "lost my patience" message.

--
Iñaki Úcar
